purpose: Per Section 9, determine the generalized root cause of the definitional candidate over-match defect (the compiled 'Acquisition' IR-definition credited as PARTIAL against three unrelated Section 1.01 definitional GT claims: doc-a::I::commitments-and-facility-sizes, doc-a::I::net-income, doc-a::I::permitted-supply-chain-financing) BEFORE any remediation, without term-specific logic.

candidateRootCausesConsidered.class: definition candidate admitted solely because term appears in nearby text
candidateRootCausesConsidered.assessment: PARTIALLY - candidate-generation.ts's pair-generation fan-out is broad by design (this is fine; Layer 4's matching.ts correctly filters most weak pairs). The defect is not that the pair was generated, but that it was subsequently classified CORRESPONDS_PARTIALLY.

candidateRootCausesConsidered.class: lexical overlap treated as semantic correspondence
candidateRootCausesConsidered.assessment: CONFIRMED - this is the root cause. See mechanism below.
NOT APPLICABLE - the defect is not a definition-to-rule linkage; it is a direct GT-claim-to-definition-candidate correspondence classification error.

candidateRootCausesConsidered.class: one definition candidate allowed to account for unrelated claims
candidateRootCausesConsidered.assessment: CONFIRMED as the observable symptom, not the cause - the SAME underlying dimension-classification mechanism (below) independently misfires for each of the three unrelated claims, since all three share the structural property that triggers it (empty action, undetermined posture).
NOT THE ROOT CAUSE - fan-out breadth is an intentional, necessary recall-maximizing design (Layer 4 is supposed to filter it); the defect is in the filter, not the fan-out.

confirmedRootCause.mechanism: IDENTICAL to the mechanism identified in 02-safe-surfacing-correspondence-spec.json for the safe-surfacing false-positive cluster. All three affected GT claims (commitments-and-facility-sizes, net-income, permitted-supply-chain-financing) are unitType DEFINITION with purely enumerative/factual descriptions (dollar amounts, dates, defined-term cross-references) that yield no clean action verb and no restrictive/permissive posture signal on extraction - both A_SUBJECT_ACTION and B_LEGAL_POSTURE resolve to NOT_APPLICABLE for these claims. This leaves C_OBJECT_RESOURCE (lexical shared-term overlap, normalized against the smaller of the two term sets) as the SOLE dimension deciding correspondence against the 'Acquisition' IR-definition candidate - which shares generic Section-1.01-definitional vocabulary (defined-term cross-references, common credit-agreement boilerplate) with all three claims despite being substantively about a different concept (M&A transactions) in each case.
confirmedRootCause.whyTheSameCandidateHitsThreeUnrelatedCla: The 'Acquisition' definition candidate is short and its extracted content-term set is correspondingly small; overlapDetail's coefficient (sharedCount / min(setA, setB)) is inflated whenever the SMALLER set is small, so a handful of shared boilerplate terms clears the threshold against ANY claim with a similarly small, weakly-specified term set - which is precisely what a definitional GT claim with no action/posture signal produces. This is a structural property of the scoring formula interacting with a structural property of definitional claims - not a coincidence tied to 'Acquisition' specifically, and not tied to DSGR.

generalizedRemediation.statement: A definition (or any other) candidate may contribute semantic correspondence via the object/resource dimension ALONE only when the correspondence evidence clears a materially higher bar than when at least one of the action/posture dimensions independently corroborates it. This is implemented as the SAME fix described in 02-safe-surfacing-correspondence-spec.json's generalizedFixDesign - a single change to semantic-correspondence.ts's C_OBJECT_RESOURCE assessment, keyed only on the already-computed, generic 'both A and B are NOT_APPLICABLE' pattern.
generalizedRemediation.noTermSpecificLogic: Confirmed: no reference to 'Acquisition', 'DSGR', a document ID, a section number, or a defined-term name appears anywhere in the implemented fix (05-generalized-remediation-record.json). The same code path is exercised identically for FWRG/LSB/CONMED candidates and any future document.

conclusion: The definitional over-match defect (Section 9) and the safe-surfacing false-positive cluster (Section 7) share ONE root cause, not two. A single generalized fix addresses both, and is described once in 02-safe-surfacing-correspondence-spec.json's generalizedFixDesign and implemented once in 05-generalized-remediation-record.json.
